column1: # SELECTION: match(v, p1, r1, …, d?) (G8 phase 2,
# first pattern IN ARGUMENT ORDER that `v` unifies with selects its
# result, and the result is the answer. A trailing argument — the one
# that makes the count even — is the default.
# What keeps this from becoming a conditional language: patterns are
# ordinary values matched by unifiability, there are no guards, there
# is no fallthrough, and no match without a default is an ERROR that
# names the patterns tried rather than an empty answer.
# The result is the answer, NOT `v & p & r` as the design wrote it: a
# match maps a value to another value, and under `v & r` every arm
# whose result is not already a `v` would be a contradiction — the
# design's own example among them (see the register, G8.2 departures).
# §5). A settled scrutinee carrying an effective default matches as the
# value generation will emit -- the innermost preferred value -- not as
# the still-open preference. Before this, a pattern could SELECT an arm
# by overriding the default: match(.s, destructive, true, false) beside
# "readonly" next to it. All rows parity-probed.
# ... and a PREF-FREE open disjunction is untouched: no effective
# default, so it matches by unifiability as documented.
